thread:
maya: Quick q — during yesterday's Hosted 429 spike I noticed client SDK retries were pretty aggressive. What's the recommended default for exponential backoff + idempotency behavior in our SDKs? Should the SDK auto-add an Idempotency-Key for non-streaming requests? cc @eric @jim

eric: We deliberately left idempotency opt-in. Auto-adding can hide duplicate-side effects for some callers. Recommended pattern:
- Respect Retry-After if present on 429
- Otherwise exponential backoff with full jitter (base 500ms, cap 30s)
- Max attempts default 5 or 6 depending on criticality

katie: Adding: SDKs should expose config knobs: maxRetries, baseBackoffMs, maxBackoffMs, jitterStrategy, respectRetryAfter (bool), idempotencyHeaderName. PR in progress that wires those for JS/Python.

jim: For 5xx: treat 500/502/503/504 as retryable. 501 and 4xx (except 429) are not. Also we add a circuit breaker: if N failures in M seconds, fail fast to avoid cascading. N=6/M=60s is a reasonable default but configurable.

maya: OK — what about streaming endpoints (server-sent or chunked)? Should we attempt to retry a failed stream?

eric: Don't auto-retry streaming body. Streaming usually implies non-idempotent context or complex partial-state. Instead: fail the stream and return an error with a suggested resume token when supported. Docs recommend callers implement resume logic.

katie: Exactly — SDK will throw a StreamInterruptedError with metadata {resume_token} when the server supports it. If no resume_token, caller must handle re-send; SDK should not silently re-submit.

maya: Can I get a short example of the backoff algorithm we want in the clients?

eric: Sure — pseudocode we use in the PR: 
```
function nextDelay(attempt) {
  base = 500 // ms
  cap = 30000 // ms
  // exponential: base * 2^(attempt-1) then full jitter
  raw = Math.min(cap, base * Math.pow(2, attempt - 1))
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * raw) // full jitter in [0, raw)
}
// usage: for (attempt=1; attempt<=max; attempt++) { send(); if success break; wait(nextDelay(attempt)); }
```
Also: if response has header Retry-After, parse seconds and use that (still apply min/max clamp).

jim: Also log every retry attempt with reason and attempt number — helps SRE tune thresholds. Avoid logging payloads.

siva: Question: what about duplicate billing or duplicate side effects if a user retries without idempotency? Payments are scary.

eric: For payment/charge endpoints we require idempotency server-side. API accepts Idempotency-Key & server will reject without it (400) or return error if flagged. SDK will warn on client side if trying to call a route annotated as requires-idempotency and no key provided.

katie: Implementation detail: SDK will add a small client-side-generated UUID if the caller sets autoIdempotency: true in config. But default is false. We don't force it to avoid surprising behavior.

maya: Sounds reasonable. One more: how should SDKs surface Retry-After when it exists? Return it in error object? header?

eric: Error object should include retryAfterMs as a numeric field and raw headers. So app can decide to honor or override.

katie: I've linked the PR and a short guideline in the SDK docs here: https://internal.redwood.ai/devex/retries-guidelines (draft). CI will run a small fault injection test.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-4521 to standardize SDK retry defaults + streaming-resume behavior, linked PR #387.

maya: thanks all — I'll review the PR and test with the Hosted sim env. :thumbsup:

eric: thanks — ping if you want a quick pairing to validate jitter distribution.

jim: I'll add a SLO note for retry storms.

katie: merging tomorrow if no objections.

siva: Appreciated — will coordinate with payments team about idempotency enforcement. :ok_hand:
